spec_match.rationale: The page probes the exact directional animation-trigger grammar with CSS.supports (including a must-fail bogus action) and models the spec's play-forwards/play-backwards state machine faithfully, but event-driven triggers are not in the level-1 draft, so the interaction path is a labelled Web Animations model rather than native trigger output.

interactive.rationale: Press-and-hold via pointer or keyboard swells the chip, release reverses it, repeated presses at the finished state increment a visible no-rewind counter, and a reset control restores the initial state.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card states exactly what the page does: the motivating press/release case with real syntax probes and a labelled model.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers extra same-direction events at the finished state (the core no-rewind contract), key-repeat presses, pointer cancel/blur release, mid-flight direction reversal, and an invalid-action syntax probe that must fail.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry, the play-forwards/play-backwards spec section, and the sibling basic and native-lab concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite predates this concept and cannot be edited (immutable); its directional-syntax contracts overlap but the no-rewind runtime contract is asserted via telemetry rather than the suite.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless-Chrome CDP driver on 2026-08-16 (fresh reload after final edit): press+hold reached currentTime=600/600 finished; two extra presses left it at 600ms with no-rewind=2; release reversed to 0; keyboard press/release and reset verified; zero console errors. Screenshots press-initial/press-held-finished/press-released captured and read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts animation-trigger-directional-syntax-probed on load and animation-trigger-press-no-rewind on the finished-state press path; no console noise.

design_system.rationale: Only shared CSS variables are used; accent-blue on ivory and ivory on accent-blue are ~6.9:1; held-state button overrides background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: The press control is a native button with keyboard press/release parity (Space/Enter, key-repeat handled), described by visible help text; state changes surface through a polite role=status readout and visible counters, not motion alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Stage grid collapses to one column under 700px; feature-route harness run 2026-08-16 reports desktop OK and mobile OK with no overflow and clean console/network.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the native directional trigger path once a Chrome build with parseable play-forwards/play-backwards is available to the harness
openQuestions.detail: The verification browser (Chromium 141 headless) does not parse the directional actions, so only the labelled Web Animations model path was exercised at runtime. When a Chrome 151+ build is available, drive the same sequence with the native syntax probes passing and record whether the native path holds the no-rewind contract.

guidanceConsulted.query: press and hold button interaction with animation playback and pointer events
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Connect buttons to element actions declaratively where possible and keep interactions on native controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Used a native button as the sole press surface with pointer capture (guarded), pointercancel/blur release, and explicit reset.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP driver exercised pointer, keyboard, hammering, and reset paths with zero console errors.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible status announcements for animated state changes live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce state changes through concise live regions and never rely on motion alone; keep keyboard parity for pointer interactions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: role=status polite readout mirrors every state transition; counters give a non-visual record; Space/Enter press-and-release parity implemented.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Driver read the readout text after each transition; mobile screenshot read for legibility.

summary: New additive concept answering the play-vs-replay major question: the ChromeStatus press/release motivation built with real directional syntax probes (including a must-fail case), a clearly-labelled Web Animations model of the spec state machine, a no-rewind telemetry assertion, and pointer+keyboard verified evidence.
